Pruning LLMs Like a Physicist: Block Removal as an Ising Optimization Problem Because the model literally gets shorter, block removal (also called depth pruning) buys predictable inference speedups on top of the memory savings, and it stacks cleanly with quantization, low-rank compression, and other techniques. We reformulate block selection as a constrained binary optimization (CBO) problem that maps directly onto an Ising glass, a disordered spin system with all-to-all interactions and a fixed number of「up」spins. Block removal gets much harder on modern heterogeneous architectures, where different block types are interleaved, and the Ising formulation doesn't care: a coupling is a coupling regardless of what kind of block sits at each site.
